extracted.intended_audience: offshore energy project developers (lessees/grant holders) preparing SAP, COP, or GAP submissions to BOEM
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory checklist and substantive content requirements that must be included in Site Assessment Plans (SAP), Construction and Operations Plans (COP), and General Activities Plans (GAP) submitted to BOEM to support NEPA and other statutory reviews and BOEM technical evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological and geotechnical reports (site characterization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports to define the baseline geological conditions of the seabed and provide sufficient data to develop a geologic model, assess geologic hazards, and determine feasibility of the proposed facility/site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Desktop studies to collect available data from published sources and nearby sites; (ii) Geophysical surveys with sufficient areal coverage, depth penetration, and resolution to define geological conditions of the seabed that could impact or be impacted by the project; (iii) Geotechnical investigations sufficient to ground-truth geophysical surveys, support development of a geological model, assess hazards, and provide geotechnical data for design including type and approximate dimensions of foundations; (iv) An overall site characterization report integrating findings, describing geological model, providing supporting data and recommendations. (Referenced for SAP, COP, GAP.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological survey reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation to determine presence of biological features and marine resources that could be affected by or affect proposed activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description of results of biological surveys to determine presence of live bottoms, hard bottoms, topographic features, benthic communities, migratory populations (fish, marine mammals, sea turtles, coastal and marine birds), seagrasses, plankton, fish and shellfish, and other plant life. (Required for SAP, COP, GAP.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Archaeological resources and historic properties surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveys and supporting data to identify archaeological resources and other historic properties to support NHPA review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archaeological resource and other historic property identification surveys with supporting data; BOEM may permit submission of certain subsea surveys with FDR per §585.701(a)(11) on a case-by-case basis. Also include Indigenous traditional cultural use and treaty/reserved rights information as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteorological and oceanographic (metocean) reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses to understand meteorological and oceanographic conditions at the site and identify conditions posing significant risk to the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desktop studies to collect hindcast or re-analysis model data and field measurements in sufficient detail to support design and to support analysis of wake effects, sediment mobility and scour, and navigational risks. (Required for SAP, COP, GAP.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazard information (NEPA support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on meteorology, oceanography, sediment transport, geology, and shallow geological or manmade hazards relevant to impacts analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide hazard information as part of SAP/COP/GAP submissions to assist BOEM in complying with NEPA and other laws (listed in tables at §§585.611, 585.627, 585.646).

rubrics_metrics.name: Water quality impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of turbidity, total suspended solids from construction, and impacts from vessel discharges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include estimates/analyses of turbidity and TSS due to construction and assessment of vessel discharge impacts in the NEPA-supporting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threatened or endangered species information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information necessary for ESA consultation regarding threatened or endangered species that could be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide species-specific data as needed to support ESA consultation (listed as a required topic in NEPA support tables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive biological resources or habitats
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and description of essential fish habitat, refuges, preserves, special management areas, marine protected areas, sanctuaries, rookeries, hard bottom habitat, chemosynthetic communities, calving grounds, barrier islands, beaches, dunes, and wetlands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe proximity and potential impacts to sensitive habitats and resources; include state and federal coastal and marine protected areas and nearby national marine sanctuaries/monuments where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous and treaty-reserved rights and traditional cultural uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on archaeological resources, other historic property use, Indigenous traditional cultural use, or use pertaining to treaty and reserved rights with Native Americans or other Indigenous peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data to enable BOEM review under NHPA and other applicable laws or policies, including information on treaty and reserved rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and economic conditions/resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of socioeconomic conditions and uses that could be affected by the proposed activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include employment, existing offshore/coastal infrastructure (major sources of supplies, services, energy, water), land use, subsistence resources and harvest practices, recreation, recreational and commercial fishing (typical seasons, location, type), minority and lower income groups, coastal zone management programs, and a visual impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coastal and marine uses and navigational safety risk assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of other ocean uses (military, vessel traffic, fisheries, other resource exploration/development) and a navigational safety risk assessment describing predicted impacts and avoidance/minimization measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a navigational safety risk assessment describing predicted impacts to navigation and measures to avoid/minimize adverse impacts. This document must also be submitted to the U.S. Coast Guard to assist its analysis if the proposal identifies potential impediments to safe navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency Certification under the Coastal Zone Management Act (CZMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: When required by CZMA, submit the appropriate consistency certification following 15 CFR part 930 subparts D or E depending on pre- or post-lease submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If SAP/COP submitted before lease issuance: 15 CFR part 930, subpart D applies; if after lease issuance: 15 CFR part 930, subpart E applies. For COP specifically, submit one copy of the consistency certification under 16 U.S.C. 1456(c)(3)(B) and 15 CFR 930.76 or 16 U.S.C. 1456(c)(3)(A) and 15 CFR 930.57 and include 'necessary data and information' per 15 CFR 930.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other resources, conditions, and activities as identified by BOEM
rubrics_metrics.description: Any additional resources, conditions, or activities BOEM identifies as relevant to NEPA or other federal reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may request additional information beyond the listed topics; include 'other' items as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP/COP/GAP NEPA information requirement (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SAP, COP, or GAP must contain detailed information and analysis to assist BOEM in complying with NEPA and other applicable laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing activities in areas BOEM has no previous experience, include the tabled topics (hazard info, water quality, biological resources, threatened species, sensitive habitats, archaeological resources, social/economic, coastal/marine uses, consistency certification, other resources) as appropriate per §§585.611 (SAP), 585.627 (COP), and 585.646 (GAP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing and procedures for CZMA consistency review
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for furnishing copies of SAP/COP and consistency certifications to State CZMA agencies and BOEM depending on before/after lease issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before lease issuance: furnish copy of SAP, consistency certification, and necessary data to applicable State CZMA agencies per 15 CFR part 930 subpart D and submit copy to BOEM per §585.110. After lease issuance: submit to BOEM pursuant to 15 CFR part 930 subpart E only if BOEM did not consider proposed activities under a previous consistency determination; BOEM will forward to State agencies after BOEM determines all information requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disapproval, notification, and resubmission process
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM disapproves a SAP/COP/GAP, BOEM will inform the applicant of the reasons and allow an opportunity to submit a revised plan; BOEM may suspend the lease/review period to allow resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM will inform reasons for disapproval and allow resubmission; suspension of lease or COP review period may occur as appropriate to give reasonable time to submit revised plan (§585.613(e)(2) and §585.628(f)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex or significant facilities — subpart H and Safety Management System
rubrics_metrics.description: If installing facilities deemed complex or significant by BOEM, applicant must comply with subpart H requirements and submit a Safety Management System description prior to construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complex/significant facilities as provided in §585.613(a)(1), compliance with subpart H and submission of the Safety Management System description required by §585.810 is mandatory before construction may begin (§585.614(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: When you must notify BOEM or revise plans (change management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to notify BOEM before conducting any site assessment or project activities not described in the approved plan; BOEM will determine whether a revision is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify BOEM in writing describing proposed activities; BOEM may request additional information to determine need for revision. If revision required, BOEM will reassess complexity/significance and may require compliance with §585.614(b) for complex/significant facilities (§585.617(a)-(b) and §585.634(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of activities likely requiring a revision to SAP/COP/GAP
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific circumstances that likely trigger a required revision to an approved plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (1) Activities not described in approved plan; (2) Modifications to number, size, or type of facilities or equipment; (3) Changes in geographical location or layout of bottom disturbances, offshore facilities, or onshore support bases beyond described ranges; (4) Structural failure of any facility; (5) Submission of FDR or FIR that contains new information or is inconsistent with the COP; (6) Change in any other activity specified by BOEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM periodic review of activities under approved plans
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will periodically review activities conducted under an approved plan; frequency and extent based on significance of information or condition changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If review indicates plan should be revised to meet requirements, BOEM will require submission of needed revisions (§585.617(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval criteria for plan revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards BOEM will apply when determining whether to approve a proposed revision to a plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may approve a revision if it is (1) designed not to cause undue harm or damage to natural resources, life (including human and wildlife), property, the marine/coastal/human environment, or sites/structures/objects of historical or archaeological significance; and (2) is otherwise consistent with the provisions of section 8(p) of the OCS Lands Act (§585.617(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decommissioning and site clearance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations to decommission site assessment facilities and projects upon lease termination or completion of commercial operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must decommission site assessment facilities as set forth in subpart J upon termination of lease and submit decommissioning application per §§585.905 and 585.906. Upon completion of commercial operations approved in COP or FERC license, decommission project per subpart J (§585.618(e), §585.638(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: COP demonstration requirements (what COP must show)
rubrics_metrics.description: The COP must demonstrate that you have planned and are prepared to conduct proposed activities consistent with statutory, safety, and environmental obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COP must demonstrate that you: (a) conform to responsibilities in §585.105(a); (b) conform to all applicable laws, regulations, and lease provisions; (c) are safe; (d) do not unreasonably interfere with other uses of the OCS, including national security/defense; (e) do not cause undue harm or damage to natural resources, life, property, the marine/coastal/human environment, or historical/archaeological sites; (f) use best available and safest technology; (g) use best management practices; and (h) use properly trained personnel (§585.621).

rubrics_metrics.name: COP project-specific information requirements (contents list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive list of project-specific items that must be included in a COP (may be provided using a PDE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes (as applicable): contact information; designation of operator; lease stipulations and compliance; location plat/indicative layout (ranges of surface locations and water depths, anchor/mooring data, existing structures); general structural/project design, fabrication and installation; deployment activities and safety/environmental protection measures; list of solid and liquid wastes and disposal methods; listing of chemical products when stored volume exceeds EPA reportable quantities (volumes, handling, transfers, disposal); description of vessels/vehicles/aircraft supporting activities and frequency/duration; general operating procedures and systems (normal and accidents/emergencies); decommissioning and site clearance procedures; listing of all Federal/State/local authorizations/approvals required; proposed measures for avoiding/minimizing/reducing/eliminating/monitoring environmental impacts (including mitigation required by subpart I); information incorporated by reference and public availability; list of agencies/persons consulted with contact info and issues discussed; references/bibliographic list; financial assurance statements (bond or other instrument per §§585.516 and 585.525–585.529); project verification strategy identifying complex/significant facilities and strategy for compliance with §§585.705–585.714; construction schedule showing milestones; air quality information as described in §585.659; and other information as required by BOEM (§585.626(a)(1)–(21)).

rubrics_metrics.name: COP required survey and investigation reports (topic coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: COP must include reports that document results of surveys and investigations to characterize and model the project site across key topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must address: geological and geotechnical (desktop, geophysical, geotechnical, overall site characterization); biological; archaeological resources and other historic properties (with possibility to submit subsea surveys with FDR per §585.701(a)(11)); and meteorological and oceanographic (metocean) desktop and field measurement studies sufficient to support preliminary design and analyses of wake, sediment mobility, scour, and navigational risks (§585.626(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: COP consistency and oil spill response documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: COP must include required CZMA consistency certification and an oil spill response plan when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit one copy of consistency certification meeting statutory/regulatory citation requirements (16 U.S.C. 1456(c)(3)(A)/(B); 15 CFR 930) and 'necessary data and information' per 15 CFR 930.58. Submit an oil spill response plan in compliance with 33 U.S.C. 1321 and include information identified in 30 CFR part 254 applicable to activities (§585.627(b)–(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project easement terms and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and conditions under which BOEM will grant and specify project easements related to COPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If BOEM approves a project easement, BOEM will issue an addendum specifying terms. Project easement must provide sufficient off-lease area to accommodate potential changes for locating cables, pipelines, and appurtenances. Unused portions may be relinquished after construction. Conditions: rights granted will not prevent later granting of other rights provided subsequent authorizations do not unreasonably interfere with approved operations; if easement in area with prior lease/ROW/RUE, easement holder must agree not to interfere with or impede existing operations (§585.628(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement of commercial operations criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which commercial operations may commence on a commercial lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If activities do not require a FERC license (e.g., wind projects), commence 30 calendar days after: (1) project verification report is deemed submitted by BOEM (§§585.704 & 585.708(a)(5)); (2) BOEM confirmed receipt of critical safety systems commissioning records (§585.708(a)(6)); and (3) BOEM has not notified objections in that timeframe. If activities require a FERC license/exemption, commence as permitted by license. Must notify BOEM within 10 business days after commencing commercial operations (§585.637).

rubrics_metrics.name: GAP approval and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for submission and approval of a General Activities Plan before commencing activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must submit your GAP to BOEM pursuant to §585.110 and receive BOEM approval of your GAP before you can begin any proposed activities on your lease or grant (§585.642, §585.640(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: GAP content requirements (what GAP must demonstrate and include)
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP must demonstrate planning and preparedness and include project-specific information similar to COP but tailored to site assessment or technology testing activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP must demonstrate conformity to §585.105(a), applicable laws/regulations/lease provisions, safety, non-interference with other OCS uses, avoidance of undue harm to natural resources/life/property/environment/historical sites, use of best available and safest technology, best management practices, and properly trained personnel (§585.641). GAP must include (as applicable): contact info, operator designation, site assessment/technology testing concept (objectives, description of proposed activities, technology, schedule), ROW/RUE/limited lease stipulations if known, location plat, general structural/project design, deployment activities and safety/environment measures, proposed measures to avoid/minimize/monitor environmental impacts, list of wastes and disposal methods, chemical product listing if volumes exceed EPA reportable quantities, description of vessels/vehicles/aircraft and frequency/duration, reference information, decommissioning/site clearance procedures, air quality info, listing of required Federal/State/local authorizations, list of agencies/persons communicated with, financial assurance info, project verification strategy analysis, information incorporated by reference and other information requested by BOEM (§585.645(a)–(20)).

rubrics_metrics.name: GAP required survey reports and additional requirements for complex projects
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP must include the same categories of site characterization reports as COP and additional details when applying for project easements or constructing complex/significant facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must cover geological/geotechnical (desktop, geophysical, geotechnical, site characterization), biological, archaeological resources/other historic properties, and metocean topics (§585.645(b)). If applying for a project easement or constructing complex/significant facilities, provide additional information and comply with subpart H, including construction and operation concept; all cables and pipelines (location, design, installation, testing, maintenance, safety devices, corrosion protection, inspections, decommissioning); general operating procedures and systems (normal and accidents/emergencies); construction schedule; and other information requested (§585.645(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project verification strategy and complexity determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to list all facilities considered complex or significant and describe strategy for compliance with project verification and safety requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COP/GAP must include a project verification strategy listing facilities or combinations considered complex/significant and describe strategy for compliance with §§585.705–585.714. For GAP, provide analysis supporting recommendation whether activities should be determined complex or significant and, if so, describe compliance strategy (§585.626(a)(18); §585.645(a)(18)).
